title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing Española after a July 23 traffic stop. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, was driving with her 12-year-old sister when a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, confusing a final 2 for a 7 and flagging the car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Officers stopped them on Calle Duran, handcuffed both sisters, and placed them in separate police vehicles before realizing the error. Jaclynn had asked police to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but officers instead handcuffed the child.

The lawsuits, filed January 3 in state District Court, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, a 17-year-old honor student who was wrongly stopped in a similar mistake involving a camera. The city of Española, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The cases will now proceed in court, with no response yet from the city.
